# rmux 0.1.20
Fix Cmd+K stopping unexpectedly and make shell exits close consistently after startup.
- Cmd+K no longer gets stuck after ignored terminal title, working-directory, or oversized control messages. Clearing still waits safely for incomplete messages to finish or cancel. - Interactive shells that have run for at least two seconds now close on exit regardless of their final status, including Ctrl+D after a failed command. Successful exits close immediately. - Failures within the first two seconds and explicitly launched commands stay open for inspection. Ctrl+D inside a running application continues to reach that application normally. - Tab closure waits for buffered output, cleans up empty panes and windows, and leaves unrelated sessions running.
Addresses the reproducible Cmd+K failure reported in [#12](https://github.com/rmuxapp/rmux/issues/12).
## Downloads
Signed and notarized macOS Apple Silicon DMG and ZIP, Linux x86-64 tarball, and Windows x86-64 ZIP. macOS updates use Sparkle. All release builds run on GitHub.
Validation: all 148 active terminal tests, the desktop debug build, and live RPC smoke checks passed. Regression coverage includes split control messages, message cancellation, startup failure retention, Ctrl+D forwarding, nonzero shell exits, and empty-window cleanup. Native Windows runtime validation remains deferred.
